reason: PC-GNN completed two verified GPU training epochs on Elliptic via a single-relation homogeneous adapter with a chronological (time-ordered) split, as required by the plan's Elliptic exception. Three source-code registrations were required: (1) a load_data() branch in utils.py reading Elliptic.mat plus single-relation adjacency pickles; (2) an eligible_index branch in unified_model_handler.py excluding the -1 (unknown-label) sentinel by value rather than by fixed index range, since Elliptic's 77.15% unlabeled nodes are scattered throughout the array rather than contiguous like Amazon's; (3) a fraud-count print-statement fix (labels==1 instead of raw sum) that is safe for all datasets and specifically necessary for any dataset with a -1 label value. None of these changes altered the PC-GNN architecture, loss, Pick-and-Choose sampling, or relation aggregators.
chronological_split_note: Validation and test are FIXED chronological blocks (timesteps [21, 32] and [33, 49]) and are IDENTICAL across all four ratios. Only the training pool (timesteps [1, 20]) is nested-subsampled (seed 2). Known fraud-rate drift across time observed: training region ~9.4%, validation ~16.2%, test ~6.5% — this is a documented property of the Elliptic dataset (fraud activity is non-uniform over time), not a split-generation defect. Validation-set metrics during tuning should not be assumed representative of test-set performance for this dataset specifically.

code_changes.reason: Registers Elliptic's file paths; mirrors existing Yelp/Amazon/T-Finance pattern.

code_changes.change: Added elif args.data_name == 'elliptic' branch: eligible_index = list(np.where(labels != -1)[0])
code_changes.reason: Elliptic has a -1 unknown-label sentinel scattered throughout the array (unlike Amazon's contiguous unlabeled range); eligibility must be determined by label value, not index range.

code_changes.change: Changed int(np.sum(labels)) to int(np.sum(labels == 1)) in the fraud-count print statement
code_changes.reason: Summing raw labels silently produces a wrong count for any dataset with a -1 sentinel; this fix is safe and behavior-identical for all existing datasets.

gadbench_cross_check: GADBench reports 9.8% anomaly rate; empirical labeled-only rate here is 9.76% — consistent.
